title: Think of your marketing budget as a financial portfolio, not time-boxed campaigns
summary: Cody argues digital marketing should drop campaigns with start and end dates (a military idea from Madison Avenue) and instead run an always-on portfolio. Spread resources across short and long term assets, favor things that compound, and simply do more of what works and less of what doesn't.

principles.text: Eliminate start and end dates; digital feedback loops are instant, so don't flight ads.
principles.quote: We need to eliminate start and end dates. I mean this as bluntly as I can, if your agency is flighting digital ads you should fire them.

principles.text: Treat the marketing budget like a financial portfolio with both short and long term initiatives, favoring what compounds.
principles.quote: Financial portfolios have both short and long term initiatives, and your marketing budget should as well.

principles.text: Don't reset your marketing to zero each year; build initiatives that grow in value over time.
principles.quote: Let’s build digital marketing initiatives into marketing portfolios that mitigate risk and grow in value over time.

principles.text: Match risk tolerance to digital maturity: early-stage digital companies can risk more, mature ones have more to lose.
principles.quote: companies who are in the early phases of adopting digital have less to lose so they should have a higher risk tolerance.

principles.text: Treat SEO as the long-term compounding investment, like income you put into accounts that compound.
principles.quote: SEO is our long-term investment. It’s our 10% yearly income that goes into accounts that have compounded growth.

principles.text: Run everything open-ended: stop what isn't working, do more of what is.
principles.quote: We don’t flight ads, we don’t do unnecessary work, we just do more of what’s working and less of what isn’t.
